excerpt: Roofstock is an Oakland platform for buying, managing and selling single-family rental homes, with Mynd and Stessa among its brands. Funding, layoffs and alternatives.
content:
Roofstock is a platform for single-family rental (SFR) and build-to-rent investors. It started as an online marketplace where people could buy rental homes, often with tenants already in place, in markets far from where they live. It now describes itself as one place to run residential portfolios from acquisition to exit, with services for acquisitions, property management, asset management, dispositions and valuations. Its brands include Mynd for full-service property management, Stessa, free software for landlords to track rental income and expenses, and RentPrep for tenant screening. Its homepage claims 400,000 users, 50 markets and $10 billion transacted.

Roofstock is based in Oakland, California. In March 2022 it raised a $240 million Series E led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 at a valuation just under $2 billion, with Khosla Ventures, Lightspeed and Bain Capital Ventures among its investors, CRETech reported. The housing slowdown hit soon after: HousingWire reported that it cut about 20% of staff in October 2022, and TechCrunch reported a second round of layoffs of about 27% in March 2023, when CEO Gary Beasley pointed to the difficult market and the need to reduce cash burn.

Roofstock does not publish one price list; its fees depend on the service, so check the relevant page before buying or listing a property. It suits investors who want to own US rental homes remotely, while local investors may prefer a local agent.

We have not used Roofstock for this page. It brings together Roofstock's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
